title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equations: Symmetries, superposition, and classicality from a Bohmian perspective
summary: Interference is commonly regarded as the most direct manifestation of the superposition principle. This association is natural for the linear Schrödinger equation, where coherent alternatives combine at the level of probability amplitudes. However, the situation becomes less transparent when nonlinear couplings are present, or when the field is only partially coherent. In this work, we argue that a more robust organizing principle is provided by the local flow generated by phase variations.
